title: Premiere Pro Beginner Tutorial: End-to-End Video Editing in 2026 (Think Media)
summary: Think Media’s complete beginner guide walks viewers through a full end-to-end workflow for editing a video in Adobe Premiere Pro (2026 era). The tutorial emphasizes upfront organization (A-roll, B-roll, assets), project setup and workspace configuration, media import into clearly named bins, creating and organizing a sequence, and performing core edits with keyboard shortcuts. It demonstrates overlaying B-roll on a multi-track timeline, applying speed changes for slow-motion on 60fps footage, and refining audio with a three-track mix, then adding titles, motion, and color correction via Lumetri and LUTs. The presenter also covers workflow efficiencies such as color-coding sections, editing the source footage to propagate color changes, white balance tweaks, and exporting with common presets. A sponsorship segment for Story Blocks is included, and the video provides downloadable project files for follow-along.
topics: Organize media into A-roll, B-roll, and assets
Create a Premiere Pro project and folder structure
Use workspaces to optimize editing
Import media and create bins for organization
Create and name a sequence from A-roll
Drag A-roll to drop media to create a sequence
Rename and organize sequences into a dedicated bin
Cut and trim with Razor (C) and Selection (V) tools
Ripple edits to shift timeline content efficiently (Q)
In and out points for selecting clip sections (I/O)
Layer A-roll and B-roll for multi-track edits
Color code timeline sections to map story beats
Insert B-roll using video-only drag to avoid overwriting audio
Slow down 60fps B-roll on a 24fps timeline
Keyboard shortcuts and remapping in Premiere
Audio workflow: three-track arrangement (voice, effects, music)
Adjusting audio levels with the Gain tool (G)
Inserting an intro bumper and aligning it with edits
Text titles: adding and styling with T, font choice, and drop shadow
Transform keyframes for motion and easing (scale)
Lumetri color correction, exposure/contrast/shadows, and white balance
Applying LUTs for color grading via the Creative tab
Color correct source footage to apply globally across clips
Export workflow: Outpoints, Command M, H.264, and 4K presets
Managing export outputs in an 'exports' folder with versioning
Sponsor: Story Blocks and its stock footage library
